key_insight: OMatG-FC generates inorganic crystals by learning atomic species and cell volume on fixed structural frameworks, achieving a reported state-of-the-art stable, unique, and novel (S.U.N.) rate below the convex hull.
engineering_relevance: Framework conditioning reduces generation dimensionality and offers a route to candidate materials without learning atomic packings from scratch.
method: Fix fractional atomic coordinates and unit-volume lattice vectors.
Generate atomic species with discrete flow matching and cell-volume scaling with stochastic interpolants.
Explore chemical assignments that can yield unseen stable prototypes from known frameworks.
evidence_signal: The authors analyze duplicate frameworks in MP-20, provide a framework-based split, and benchmark OMatG-FC with LeMat-GenBench using three machine-learning interatomic potentials.
watch_item: Generation remains constrained by the supplied frameworks, and predicted stability requires validation beyond machine-learning interatomic potentials.
